To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We report the first description of a patient with mosaic pancreatic islet disease caused by two independent somatic genetic events: a heterozygous ABCC8 mutation in a subset of β‐cells and paternal uniparenteral disomy in all islet cells.
• A patient with CHI was found to have a localised area within the pancreas associated with marked islets hypertrophy and a distinct histological appearance from diffuse and focal CHI.

we have discovered the genetic cause of mosaic congenital hyperinsulinaemia in a patient with focal disease and have shown that the disease is caused by the presence of two separate genetic mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the causes of hypoglycaemic conditions, which are often life-threatening.
understanding the genetic causes of congenital hyperinsulinaemia, a disorder that causes life‐threatening low blood sugar.
understanding the genetic causes of congenital hyperinsulinaemia (CHI) and how these cause islet cell disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic cause of the patient's CHI was a de‐novomutation in exon 27 of ABCC8 (c. 3378G>A, p.Glu1126Lys), and that the mutation was present in a mosaic state in the islets of the tail of the patient's pancreas.
this is the first report of a de novo mosaic somatic genetic lesion causing CHI.
a de novo mosaic mutation in ABCC8 in the presence of mosaic paternal unipaternal disomy is the underlying genetic cause of localised mosaic CH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a patient with mosaic pancreatic disease caused by two independent genetic mutations.
we have identified two genetic lesions within a single patient with CHI which are not present within the rest of the body.
the genetic basis of CHI is not always as straightforward as we may expect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mosaic pancreatic disease in CHI is caused by a somatic mosaic ABCC8 gene mutation in combination with paternal uniparentel disomy.
mosaic disease in CHI can result from two separate genetic lesions occurring independently within the islets of the pancreas.
the genetic cause of CHI is not always the same.
